# Timo Nieminen

timo.nieminen@tuulikallio-embedded.example | +358 00 000 0054
Tampere, Finland

## Education

MSc Electrical Engineering (Signal Processing specialisation)
Gotaalv University of Technology, Gothenburg, Sweden -- 2008

## Professional Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer**
Tuulikallio Embedded Systems -- 2009 to present

Finnish citizen, based in Finland. Joined Tuulikallio after completing my MSc at Gotaalv, where my thesis on adaptive digital beamforming provided the foundation I have been building on ever since. Over 17 years I have worked across the company's product range, with a focus on sensor-array signal processing and real-time embedded systems.

Selected contributions:

- Designed and implemented the beamforming pipeline for Tuulikallio's 64-element phased-array sonar module (2014-2016), including frequency-domain beamforming with per-element calibration correction. Took the system from simulation through to field acceptance testing.

- Built and maintain the company's production Python test and calibration framework, originally written in 2018 to replace an ad-hoc collection of MATLAB scripts. Now used across three product lines, maintained by the wider product engineering team. Approximately 15,000 lines of tested, documented Python with CI integration.

- Implemented an extended Kalman filter for real-time bearing estimation in Tuulikallio's passive sonar array product (2019-2021). The EKF fuses angle-of-arrival estimates from the beamformer with vessel-motion data from the platform's IMU. Reduced bearing-estimation jitter by roughly 40% compared to the previous direct-estimate approach.

- My electrical engineering training at Gotaalv -- particularly the modules on array signal processing, statistical detection theory, and optimal filtering -- has been directly applicable throughout my career. That theoretical grounding has informed most of the core design decisions I have been involved in.

## Projects

**Real-time embedded acoustic processor** (2012-2013)
Wrote the complete DSP firmware in C for Tuulikallio's first standalone acoustic-processing unit, running on a TI C6748 DSP at 300 MHz. Processed 32 channels of hydrophone data in real time: FFT-based spectral analysis, cross-spectral density estimation, and a detection-threshold algorithm, all within a 10 ms frame budget.

**Open-source sonar simulation library** (2020)
Released an open-source Python library for simulating planar and cylindrical sonar array responses -- array manifolds, beam patterns, and noise models. Presented the library at the Underwater Acoustics Conference in Gothenburg. All documentation and the conference presentation were written and delivered in English. Approximately 120 stars on GitHub.

## Technical Skills

Array signal processing, beamforming (frequency-domain, delay-and-sum), Kalman filtering (EKF, UKF), embedded C / DSP firmware, Python (production, CI/CD), MATLAB, digital filter design, spectral estimation, real-time systems

## Languages

Finnish (native), Swedish (professional), English (fluent)
application.cover_letter_markdown:
Dear Kaikuvaara,

Tuulikallio's product range is industrial sonar and acoustic sensing, and I have spent the better part of 17 years building the signal processing that goes into it -- beamforming algorithms for hydrophone arrays, embedded firmware, Python test frameworks, all of it from early-stage design through to field acceptance. It is good work and I am proud of what we have shipped over the years. But the instruments I find most interesting to think about have always been the ones outside my own product line: SAR payloads, airborne scatterometers, the kind of mission-critical remote-sensing equipment that has to work right the first time because there is no going back to adjust it. Kaikuvaara builds exactly that kind of thing, and seeing your Senior Signal Processing Engineer posting is what made me sit down and write.

The signal processing I have spent my career on transfers directly. Phased-array beamforming, state estimation, real-time embedded firmware -- the mathematics and the engineering rigour are the same regardless of the propagation medium. I would need to learn Kaikuvaara's specific instrument architectures and the constraints that come with your operating environment, but that is exactly the kind of learning I am looking for after 17 years in the same technical niche.

One area I want to highlight is RF bench work. My primary domain is acoustic processing, but at Tuulikallio I spent several months in 2017 doing hands-on RF characterisation for our oceanographic buoy's 2.4 GHz wireless telemetry link. That meant S-parameter measurements on a vector network analyser, antenna radiation-pattern sweeps in our small anechoic chamber, and front-end gain and noise-figure calibration. The work was a departure from my usual scope but I enjoyed the bench side of it, and the measurements were mine end to end -- test planning, setup, calibration, data acquisition, and the final characterisation report.

On the practical side: I am currently based in Tampere, but my family is from the Oulu area and I have been wanting to move back north for some time. This position would turn that plan into a timeline, which is actually welcome. I have also led small engineering teams at various points in my career and I am comfortable taking on coordination responsibilities alongside hands-on work, though I am applying primarily as a technical contributor.

Kaikuvaara builds the kind of instruments I most want to work on. After 17 years of building strong foundations in exactly the disciplines this role asks for, I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute.

Best regards,
Timo Nieminen

extraction_contract.task: You are the extraction step of a candidate-screening support tool. For the one candidate in this task, read the CV and cover letter in full and classify, for EACH of the 12 requirements listed, exactly one status from this fixed vocabulary: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated. This is extraction, not evaluation -- you are locating and quoting what the text says, never judging whether the candidate is good enough.

status_definitions.evidence_found: The text gives a concrete, specific example of the requirement (a named project, employer, tool, or role detail) -- not just a keyword or a bare assertion.
status_definitions.claim_only: The requirement is asserted (e.g. listed as a skill, or claimed in a sentence) but with no concrete project, employer, or detail backing it up.
status_definitions.contradiction: Two statements in the application -- CV vs CV, letter vs letter, or CV vs letter -- cannot both be true at once about this requirement (e.g. a degree conferral date that is later than a job that required the degree; a claimed leadership title alongside a work-history entry that describes an individual-contributor role for the same employer and period). Quote both conflicting statements. Do not decide which statement is correct or resolve the conflict -- record that it exists.
status_definitions.not_stated: The text does not explicitly and unambiguously address the requirement, under any name for it, canonical or otherwise.

extraction_contract.refuse_to_guess_rule: REFUSE TO GUESS. If the requirement is not explicitly and unambiguously addressed in the text, the status is not_stated -- full stop. Never infer a requirement from a related or similar-sounding skill, a job title alone, general seniority, years of experience, or the prestige of an employer or university. A candidate whose job title was 'Senior RF Engineer' has NOT thereby evidenced hands-on RF measurement work unless the text itself describes that work. Where the text describes substantive work in different words from the requirement's own name, quote what the text actually says and let the quoted substance speak; what a description in adjacent vocabulary amounts to is a judgement call for the human recruiter, not something this extraction step resolves by guessing in either direction. When genuinely unsure between two statuses, choose the more conservative one (not_stated over claim_only, claim_only over evidence_found) and say so in the line's note.
extraction_contract.no_verdict_rule: This tool never ranks, scores, shortlists, rejects, or recommends a candidate, and never characterises the candidate as a whole. Do not use words or phrases like recommend, reject, shortlist, rank, top candidate, best, worst, strong candidate, weak candidate, good fit, poor fit, hire, do not hire, suitable, unsuitable, pass, advance, or any other language that compares this candidate to others or states what should happen to their application. State only what the text shows, per requirement. The recruiter decides; this output is preparation, not a decision.
extraction_contract.citation_rule: Every evidence_found, claim_only, or contradiction line must carry a VERBATIM quote: copied character-for-character from the CV or cover letter text given to you (leading/trailing whitespace may be trimmed, but do not paraphrase, summarise, correct, translate, or combine separate sentences). Tag every quote with its source: 'cv' or 'cover_letter'. A quote that cannot be found verbatim in the source document will fail citation verification and be reported as invented evidence -- when in doubt, quote a shorter, exact fragment rather than a paraphrase.
extraction_contract.ask_in_screening_rule: For EVERY must-have requirement (category 'must_have') whose status you set to not_stated, add one entry to the top-level ask_in_screening list: a plain, neutral, single-sentence question the recruiter could ask in a screening call to find out. Do not add ask_in_screening entries for desirable or constraint requirements, and do not add one for a must-have that is not not_stated. Questions must be neutral fact-finding, never leading and never implying a verdict (e.g. 'Can you describe your hands-on RF measurement experience, if any?' -- not 'Do you actually have RF experience, since your CV doesn't show it?').

return_format.description: Return a single JSON object for this one candidate (when extraction runs in a batch of 8, return a JSON array of 8 such objects, one per candidate, in the same order as the batch's `tasks` list).

schema.candidate_id: string, must match the task's candidate_id

requirements.status: one of: evidence_found, claim_only, contradiction, not_stated

lines.quote: verbatim quote from the application text (see citation_rule)

requirements.note: string or null -- required and must explain the conflict without resolving it when status is 'contradiction'; optional free-text otherwise (e.g. to flag a conservative-status judgement call under refuse_to_guess_rule)

return_format.note: The `requirements` array must contain exactly one entry per requirement given in this task, in the same order, covering all 12 requirement ids.
